newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesian journalists group says coverage hampered.
newsitem.headline: Indonesian journalists group says coverage hampered.

text.p: An independent journalist group said on Wednesday that Indonesian security officers hampered reporters while they were covering campaign rallies for the May 29 general election.

The Alliance of Independent Journalists (AJI) said in a report it had recorded a number of instances in which police and soldiers had hampered journalists, including cases of assault and the seizing of film and videotape.

"Our findings indicate that most of the violations were committed by security officers, either police or soldiers. There were also violations committed by the participants of the campaign rallies," AJI secretary-general Satrio Arismunandar told Reuters.
The report, which mainly included incidents on the main island of Java, was submitted to the National Commission of Human Rights.

The report quoted an incident in which plain-clothes security officers seized videotape from a Reuters cameraman and another video photographer during the campaign. Film belonging to a Reuters photographer was also seized.
In another case, plain-clothes security officers kicked the stomach of a photographer during a street clash in south Jakarta two weeks ago, the AJI said.

A photographer was beaten by security officers while covering a clash in east Jakarta because the officers believed he was a member of the banned left-wing youth group, the People's Democratic Party (PRD), the report said.
The unrecognised AJI was formed in 1994 after two magazines and a weekly tabloid were banned. It says it has 80 members.
Two members of the group are serving three-year jail terms for insulting the government in an AJI bulletin.
"I believe we have to create a situation in which journalists can do their jobs freely...so that we can be good observers for the general elections," said Arismunandar.
